Show me a simple example of web wire-call verbs (the live fetch) in Motoi Scheme.

```motoi
;; SITUATION: search the web for current retail price of a competitor's item
;; ROUTE: call web/search, extract a price if present
(define (check-competitor-price query)
  (let ((results (web/search query)))
    (if results
        (let ((price (web/extract results "price")))
          (if price
              (surface :say "Competitor price: ~a." price)
              (surface :say "Found results, but no price listed.")))
        (escalate 'service-not-yet-wired))))

(check-competitor-price "ceramic mug handmade Brooklyn")
;; prints: escalation (backing not yet wired)
```

How do I use `let` for 1.1 — a two-variable lp: maximize profit in Motoi?

```motoi
(define prob-furniture
  (ops/lp
    'maximize
    '(30 40)          ; coefficients of objective (profit per chair, per table)
    '((1 2)           ; constraint matrix: [labor, wood] × [x y]
      (4 3))
    '(8 18)           ; right-hand sides (hours, board-feet)
    '(<= <=)))        ; both constraints are ≤

(define solution (ops/lp-solve prob-furniture))

solution
; => ((x . 2) (y . 3) (value . 180))
```

What does this Motoi Scheme program do?

```motoi
(call-with-world
 (make-world width: 400 height: 400 background: '(245 245 250))
 (lambda (w)
   (let ((frame 0))
     (define (draw)
       (world-clear w)
       (let* ((t (/ frame 60.0))
              (base-squash (+ 0.8 (* 0.2 (sin (* t 2.5)))))
              (bias (sin (* t 1.5)))
              (top-squash (* base-squash (+ 1.0 (* 0.3 bias))))
              (bot-squash (* base-squash (- 1.0 (* 0.3 bias))))
              (h-scale (/ 1.0 (sqrt base-squash)))
              (v-scale (sqrt base-squash)))
         (world-draw-ellipse w 200 (- 200 30) (* 50 h-scale) (* 30 v-scale) '(180 120 140) 'fill)
         (world-draw-ellipse w 200 (+ 200 30) (* 50 h-scale) (* 30 v-scale) '(140 180 120) 'fill)
         (set! frame (+ frame 1))))
     (world-on-tick w draw 60)
     (world-show w)
     (world-wait w))))
```

How do I use `let` for pursue: seek where the target will be in Motoi?

```motoi
;; A pursuer chasing a moving target.
(define (pursue-demo)
  (let* ((w (world/spawn '()))
         (target (world/spawn w `((pos (16 12))
                                   (vel (1.5 0.5))
                                   (max-speed 2.0)
                                   (kind target))))
         (pursuer (world/spawn w `((pos (4 4))
                                    (vel (0 0))
                                    (max-speed 2.5)
                                    (kind pursuer)))))
    (ai/max-force! pursuer 0.6)
    
    ;; give the target a simple wander so it moves unpredictably
    (define (step-target)
      (let ((wander (ai/wander target 1.0 0.3)))
        (entity/accel! target (car wander) (cdr wander))))
    
    (define (draw)
      (clear-cell)
      (let ((tpos (entity/pos target))
            (ppos (entity/pos pursuer)))
        (paint-cell (car tpos) (cdr tpos) "🐇")
        (paint-cell (car ppos) (cdr ppos) "🦊")))
    
    (define (step)
      (step-target)
      (let ((steer (ai/pursue pursuer target 10)))  ; predict 10 frames ahead
        (entity/accel! pursuer (car steer) (cdr steer))
        (world/step w)))
    
    (big-bang w
              (on-tick step)
              (to-draw draw))))

(pursue-demo)
```

What does this Motoi Scheme program do?

```motoi
(world/reset!)
(define leader (world/spawn 'leader 0 0))
(define follower (world/spawn 'follower -3 -2))
(entity/set-vel! leader 2 1)
(let loop ((n 80))
  (when (> n 0)
    (let* ((leader-pos (entity/pos leader))
           (follower-pos (entity/pos follower))
           (dx (- (car leader-pos) (car follower-pos)))
           (dy (- (cadr leader-pos) (cadr follower-pos)))
           (dist (dsqrt (+ (* dx dx) (* dy dy)))))
      (when (> dist 0.1)
        (entity/set-vel! follower 
                         (* 2.5 (/ dx dist)) 
                         (* 2.5 (/ dy dist)))))
    (world/step 0.016)
    (loop (- n 1))))
(list (entity/pos leader) (entity/pos follower))
```
The second entity always moves toward the first entity's *current* position. The first moves freely; the second chases.

What does this Motoi Scheme program do?

```motoi
(define D (matrix/make (list (list 5 0)
                              (list 0 3))))

(define evals (linalg/eigenvalues D))

(list 'D D 'eigenvalues evals)
```
An **eigenvector** of a matrix A is a nonzero vector v such that **Av = λv** for some scalar λ (the **eigenvalue**). Geometrically, A stretches v by a factor of λ but doesn't change its direction.
